bullets.title: NFLX: -9-11% premarket on soft 3Q guide, FCF miss; analysts cut PTs, debate deepens
bullets.body: Netflix Q2 EPS $0.80 beat and revenue $12.56B was roughly in-line, but Q3 revenue guide of $12.86B missed consensus $13.00B, FCF came in at $1.53B vs. $2.51B estimated, and FY26 revenue range was narrowed (not raised). Shifting engagement disclosure to annual cadence amplified bears. Average sell-side PT fell ~6% to ~$106; JPM cut PT to $85 (OW), MS cut to $83 (OW), UBS to $115 (Buy), Wolfe to $84 (OP), Citi to $85 (OP), KeyBanc holds $92 (OW); KGI downgraded to Neutral with $75 PT. Core debate: UCAN deceleration, engagement plateau, and whether ad revenue ramp (~$3B in 2026) and live programming are sufficient catalysts.

bullets.title: AAPL: HSBC upgrades to Buy, raises PT to $366 from $260; stock at all-time high
bullets.body: HSBC analyst Nicolas Cote-Colisson upgraded AAPL from Hold to Buy, raising the price target to $366 from $260, implying ~10% upside from the ~$333 price at time of alert. Apple shares also reached new all-time highs intraday, approaching a $5T market cap milestone. Stock gained ~0.6% premarket on the upgrade.

bullets.title: CSCO/ANET: Morgan Stanley VAR checks show accelerating demand; CSCO OW $130 PT
bullets.body: MS 2Q26 CIO survey and VAR checks show CSCO growth expectations rose to 3.0% from 0.6%, with 67% of VARs expecting sales growth (vs. 48%) and 43% naming CSCO as best positioned for AI/DC spend. Growth is running ~11% YoY, broad-based across data center, campus, and Wi-Fi. ANET showing ~25-26% YoY growth in enterprise data center. Security is now the leading refresh driver at 53% of VARs. MS PT $130, Overweight. FFIV stable at ~7% YoY.

bullets.title: Semi/AI trade sell-off deepens: Kimi K3, positioning unwind, semis -12% in 30 days
bullets.body: China's Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 (2.8T parameter, world's largest open-weight model), ranking top-3 globally and triggering 'DeepSeek 2.0' fears about frontier AI business model viability. Semis are down ~12% over 30 days after record Q2 gains; CRWV -53%, MRVL -44%, ARM -44%, WDC -43% from 52-week highs. HF gross leverage at 99th pct but momentum not yet fully reset. Jefferies notes tech momentum drawdown exceeds dot-com era on 30-day basis. NDX futures down ~2% premarket; Asian markets closed sharply lower (Nikkei -5%, Taiwan -6%, HK Tech -5%).

bullets.title: NVDA: Bears cite Chinese model specialization on Huawei chips; Kimi K3 requires GB300/B300 for deployment
bullets.body: Jensen Huang acknowledged that Chinese AI models may specialize toward Huawei chips rather than NVIDIA hardware, posing a long-term competitive risk. Separately, Kimi K3's 2.8T parameter model cannot fit on a single NVIDIA DGX B200; deployment requires GB300 NVL72 or B300 systems with 288GB memory per GPU, which is bullish for higher-end NVDA hardware but uncertain for China access.

bullets.title: AMD: Citi/Jefferies bullish into Advancing AI 7/22-23 event; MI455X + Venice CPU catalysts
bullets.body: AMD's Advancing AI conference (July 22-23) is expected to feature the MI455X with 432GB HBM4 memory and Venice CPU on TSMC 2nm. Citi is a buyer of AMD ahead; Jefferies expects announcements with Microsoft and Anthropic on MI400 series wins. Venice CPU expected to extend leadership over Intel Granite Rapids. AMD positioned as credible GPU second-source at Meta with ramp expected 2H27/2028.

bullets.title: TXN/INTC previews: Citi sees 4-13% EPS upside for both into 7/22-23 reports
bullets.body: Citi models TXN Jun/Sep-Q EPS 1%/4% above consensus, with C26/C27 EPS $8.03/$10.10 (4-13% above Street) on industrial and data center strength. INTC 2Q26 sales modeled at $14.4B (6% QoQ), EPS $0.24 above consensus; 3Q26 upside from CPU demand and custom ASIC. INTC foundry expected to scale in 2027 via Apple, NVIDIA, MediaTek, Terafab ramp.

bullets.title: TSM: PT raises from MS ($2,988), JPM (NT$3,200), DA Davidson ($500); Q2 beat overshadowed by sector fear
bullets.body: TSMC Q2 revenue $40.2B (+33.7% YoY) at top of guidance; gross margin 67.7% beat guided 65.5-67.5%. Company raised 2026 capex to $60-64B. AI semiconductor revenue tracking above prior 55-60% CAGR—MS sees 70-80% as reasonable. Despite strong print, Taiwan-listed shares fell 3.8% intraday as foreign investors sold $5.8B of Taiwan equities (record). JPM raises FY26/27/28 EPS 4%/2%/6%.

bullets.title: NOW: Q2 earnings setup favorable; JPM and MS both see cRPO upside and federal demand
bullets.body: ServiceNow reports Q2 after the close on 7/22 (consensus EPS $0.86, revenue $3.93B). JPM flags that investors want cc cRPO growth of 18.5%+ vs. guidance of 17.5%; any 3Q subscription deceleration below 21-21.5% will disappoint. MS notes favorable setup with Federal customer demand driving upside. Key risk: customer backlash on 50-100% AI bundle pricing in renewals.

bullets.title: META: Hires top AWS exec Dave Brown for data center build-out; exploring cloud push
bullets.body: Meta has poached Dave Brown, a top Amazon Web Services executive with ~20 years of experience, to lead data center infrastructure. The hire signals Meta's ambition to build a cloud services business. MS notes a Meta cloud launch would increase colocation demand, benefiting EQIX and DLR. GOOGL also featured as a key beneficiary of Kimi K3 fragmentation, with hyperscalers positioned as orchestration layer.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Gemini 3.5 Pro delayed months; engineers frustrated about competitive gap
bullets.body: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro launch has been pushed back months beyond its May developer conference target, primarily due to coding capability shortfalls. Internal frustration is growing as engineers worry about losing ground to Anthropic and OpenAI. GOOGL closed down 4.4% Thursday, erasing ~$200B in market cap. Alphabet reports Q2 earnings July 22 after the close (consensus EPS $2.88, revenue $117.0B).

bullets.title: DELL/HPE: DELL widening server/PC/storage leadership vs HPE via supply chain execution
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley VAR call shows DELL gaining PC share YoY while HPQ lost share; DELL saw strongest QoQ storage improvement vs. peers. Hardware prices surged: servers +70% YoY, storage/PCs +50%, networking +25-30%, with ~70% of 2Q hardware revenue growth pricing-driven. ~10-15% of 2Q demand reflects pull-forward. Deployment resources identified as main constraint on further acceleration.

bullets.title: UBER: Acquires Delivery Hero at €41.50/sh (~$14.8B); antitrust close expected 2H27
bullets.body: Uber submitted an all-cash offer for Delivery Hero at €41.50/share, with Prosus (~17% stake) already committed irrevocably. The deal expands Uber's markets to 99 and cross-platform coverage to 59%. Jefferies sees little room for a price bump or counter-bid; antitrust/BaFin approvals expected to gate close to 2H27. Roth maintains Buy on UBER with $105 PT.

bullets.title: DKNG: Bet365 reaches 7.3% US OSB share in 17 states; mid-single digit threat growing
bullets.body: Bet365 now operates in 17 US states covering ~39% of US population (vs. 25.5% in Jan 2025), gaining 220bps of OSB GGR share to 7.3% in April 2026. Hold rate gap to FanDuel/DKNG narrowing. UBS sees Bet365 as a mid-single digit threat to the DraftKings/FanDuel duopoly. DKNG/FanDuel combined still hold 70%+ OSB GGR share.

bullets.title: VRT: Down 4% premarket on broad AI/tech sector weakness
bullets.body: Vertiv declined 4.0-4.7% in premarket trading, cited in both the industrials and technology sector summaries as part of the broader AI/data center infrastructure selloff. No company-specific fundamental news was cited as the driver; weakness attributed to the China AI competition narrative weighing on the full AI buildout complex.

bullets.title: BE/SEI: Morgan Stanley bullish on onsite power generation as data center buildout drives demand
bullets.body: MS identifies a 38GW US data center power shortfall through 2028 with interconnection delays extending beyond 5 years. Federal policy is shifting toward requiring large-load customers to fund their own grid upgrades, catalyzing onsite generation. SEI and BE are identified as beneficiaries. The MSXXONPW onsite power basket is down 19% in three weeks, which MS frames as an entry point.

bullets.title: NBIS: Cramer bearish near-term; trader commentary confirms weak technicals
bullets.body: Jim Cramer called NBIS 'a very good company' but said 'it's not done going down' and the current price is not a good entry. Multiple trader comments on X confirm the stock remains weak technically and needs to find a low before the neocloud sector can bounce. One trader disclosed selling at $75.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: Citi moves Fox to Top Pick on Roku deal; PT $78 and $157 respectively
bullets.body: Citi argues the market is overreacting to Fox's Roku acquisition announcement. It models ~$1B in annual EBITDA synergies (revenue + cost), FCF accretion within one year of closing vs. Fox's two-year guide, and a deal close as early as 4Q26 vs. Fox's 1H27 outlook. Fox PT maintained at $78; Roku PT raised from $120 to $157 on 90% deal probability at $161.

bullets.title: EQIX: MS Overweight at $1,250 PT; CIO survey supports colocation demand acceleration
bullets.body: MS 2Q26 CIO survey shows IT budget growth accelerating with colocation maintaining stable ~7% share of growing workloads. EQIX forecast to bring ~300MW/year online through 2029; bull case implies 15% recurring revenue growth in 2027 and $50 AFFO/share (~10% above consensus). Shares trade at 21x '27 EBITDA with ~2.2x bull/bear skew. Meta cloud launch viewed as incremental positive for EQIX interconnect demand.

bullets.title: Earnings calendar: GOOGL, TXN, NOW, T, INTC, VZ, CHTR, CMCSA all report next week
bullets.body: Key earnings next week: GOOGL (Wed 7/22 AMC, est. EPS $2.88, rev $117.0B), TXN (Wed 7/22 AMC, est. EPS $1.92), NOW (Wed 7/22 AMC, est. EPS $0.86), T (Wed 7/22 BMO), INTC (Thu 7/23 AMC, est. EPS $0.21), CMCSA (Thu 7/23 BMO), VZ (Fri 7/24 BMO), CHTR (Fri 7/24 BMO). Hyperscaler 2027 capex guidance is the key watch across GOOGL/AMZN/META calls given the AI spending debate.
